title: Surface lessons at the write boundary (guard PreToolUse hook)
description:
All four lesson anchor kinds (symbol/file/directory/import_pattern) are LOCATION keys. Greenfield code has no location yet, so lessons structurally cannot surface when writing new software. sutra_read/sutra_impact need a symbol; sutra_orient needs a component or file path that already exists in the index.

src/guard.rs already runs as a PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write and has ToolInput { file_path, content, new_string } — everything query_for_context needs (file_path, imports, project, workspace_languages). It has zero lessons integration today.

The write boundary is the right surface: it fires at the exact moment greenfield code becomes concrete, requires no directive compliance from the agent, and imports are visible before the code below them is written (killing the chicken-and-egg objection to import_pattern anchors).

acceptance_criteria.text: Writing a new file with a matching import_pattern anchor surfaces the lesson via guard advisory output
Guard never denies on lessons alone
At most 2 lessons per write, verified-first, omitted count reported
No measurable guard latency regression on writes with zero matching anchors

implementation_plan:
1. Extract imports from ToolInput content/new_string (reuse existing import-extraction if the parser exposes one; otherwise language-aware prefix scan).
2. Build lessons::MatchContext from guard's FileFacts + extracted imports.
3. Call query_for_context, budget hard: 1-2 verified lessons max, with "N more: sutra_lessons(...)" pointer.
4. Emit as ADVISORY output only — never a GuardDecision::Deny.
5. Gate behind existing guard disable env + a lessons-specific opt-out.
execution_record:
Landed as designed. Three things worth recording:

1. The guard blocked my own first edit — the `no-clone-driven-dev` forbidden_pattern rule caught `i.raw_path.clone()` when building the imports slice. Rather than waive, changed `MatchContext.imports` from `&[String]` to `&[&str]`, which removes the allocation from the hot guard path entirely and matches the "prefer slices" discipline. Cost: 2 mechanical caller updates (read.rs, context.rs build a `Vec<&str>` view over their existing `Vec<String>`) and 5 test fixtures.

2. Emission had to be threaded through four non-deny exit points rather than one tail, because a PreToolUse hook may emit only one JSON object and the existing deny paths each `println!` and return. Deny takes the channel; lessons surface on the retry after the agent acks. `parse_proposed` was hoisted above the `file_row` bail since it depends only on path+content, not file_id — that bail IS the greenfield case.

3. First cut computed the lessons lookup eagerly before the deny checks, making every denied write pay to open lessons.db (which runs migrations + archive_decayed on open). Refactored so `emit_lessons` does the lookup itself and is only called from paths that did not deny.

Observed during E2E: only 1 of ~6 lessons anchored to `directory:src/constraints` surfaced, with no "N more" line. This is Phase 4 verified-first suppression working as designed — one verified lesson sharing an anchor key silences every unverified lesson on that same key. Good for token budget, but it means a broad directory anchor with one verified lesson hides the rest. Not a regression; flagged for the ranking work in sutra/278.

Verified: 1442 tests pass, clippy clean on touched files, and five E2E hook invocations (new unindexed file → surfaces; no matching anchors → silent; load-bearing file → deny wins with single JSON object and no advisory; body-local edit → surfaces; SUTRA_GUARD_LESSONS_DISABLE=1 → silent).

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (range 6369fc3..91fedc7) — verdict: request changes.

[high] Unbounded sqlite work added to the blocking guard path (src/guard.rs lessons_for_proposed → src/lessons.rs:344-355).
Every non-denied write calls lessons_for_proposed, which opens ~/.sutra/lessons.db (create_dir_all + migrations + archive work), then query_for_context loads EVERY non-archived file/import_pattern/directory anchor for the project and filters in Rust. This fires even on zero-match writes because file_path is always Some, and a missing lessons.db is created/migrated rather than skipped. LessonsDb::open sets PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 while the installed PreToolUse hook timeout is 3000ms — a locked or slow lessons.db can eat the entire hook budget and make edits feel broken for a purely advisory feature. Verified additionally: query_for_context ends with an UPDATE lessons SET last_surfaced (a WRITE, taking the sqlite write lock) on the blocking path. Acceptance criterion "no measurable guard latency regression on writes with zero matching anchors" is not met — it is asserted, not demonstrated.
Fix: skip immediately when lessons.db does not already exist; guard-specific short busy timeout; no migrations/archive/last_surfaced writes from PreToolUse; indexed SQL candidate selection with a hard LIMIT before Rust-side glob matching.

[high] Greenfield import_pattern surfacing is silently unavailable outside Rust and Dart (src/guard.rs:405).
language_from_path only recognizes .rs and .dart. parse_proposed returns None for anything else, so imports is empty and import_pattern anchors cannot match for a new Python/TS/JS/C file — only file/directory anchors survive. That is the primary acceptance case ("writing a new file with a matching import_pattern anchor surfaces the lesson") unmet for four of six supported languages. Direct irony: sutra/280 removed the hardcoded rust/dart literal from lessons.rs while the same hardcoded pair survives here.
Fix: derive the guard language from default_registry() by extension; add guard-level Write tests for at least Python and TypeScript.

Test gap: the new tests exercise format_lesson_advisory / render_advisory_stdout in isolation. The actual PreToolUse write path (emit_lessons wiring, greenfield no-file_row branch, deny-takes-the-channel ordering) is untested end to end.
